  "findings": [

      "file": "pkg/services/anonymous/anonimpl/impl.go",
      "line": 87,
      "severity": "high",
      "category": "bug",
      "title": "Only cache devices after successful admission",
      "body": "tagDeviceUI adds the device to localCache before CreateOrUpdateDevice checks the limit. When the store returns ErrDeviceLimitReached, that cache entry remains. The next request with the same device ID returns nil from the cache lookup, so Anonymous.Authenticate grants access without checking the limit again. Every rejected device can therefore bypass the limit by retrying, for the 29-minute cache lifetime. Cache only successful admissions, and do not treat an in-flight admission as successful."
    },
    {
      "file": "pkg/services/anonymous/anonimpl/client.go",
      "line": 44,
      "severity": "medium",
      "category": "bug",
      "title": "Requests without a device header bypass the limit",
      "body": "The authentication gate relies entirely on TagDevice, but TagDevice returns nil immediately when X-Grafana-Device-Id is absent. An anonymous client can omit this client-controlled header and continue accessing Grafana APIs even when the configured device limit has been reached; no count or admission check runs. Requests subject to the limit need a server-established device identifier or another admission path rather than treating missing tracking information as successful admission."
    },
    {
      "file": "pkg/services/anonymous/anonimpl/anonstore/database.go",
      "line": 110,
      "severity": "medium",
      "category": "concurrency",
      "title": "Make counting and admitting a device atomic",
      "body": "CountDevices and the subsequent upsert execute in separate database sessions without serialization. Two requests for different new device IDs can both observe a count below deviceLimit and then both insert successfully. For example, with a limit of one and an empty table, concurrent requests can admit multiple devices, which remain eligible for updates afterward. Admission must atomically enforce the count across concurrent requests and Grafana instances."
    },
    {
      "file": "pkg/setting/setting.go",
      "line": 1654,
      "severity": "medium",
      "category": "bug",
      "title": "Register device_limit in the default configuration",
      "body": "This PR reads device_limit but does not add that key to conf/defaults.ini. Grafana's environment override pass visits keys already present in the loaded INI configuration, before readAuthSettings runs. Consequently, setting GF_AUTH_ANONYMOUS_DEVICE_LIMIT alone in a normal deployment is ignored, and this getter reads zero, silently disabling the limit. Add the key to the default configuration or read it through an environment-aware accessor."
    },
    {
      "file": "packages/grafana-runtime/src/config.ts",
      "line": 97,
      "severity": "low",
      "category": "api",
      "title": "Preserve the numeric type of anonymousDeviceLimit",
      "body": "The initializer infers this class property as undefined, not number | undefined. The exported runtime config therefore declares that anonymousDeviceLimit can never contain the number supplied by the backend, despite GrafanaConfig declaring that numeric contract. Consumers that narrow the property before using number methods get a never type and cannot type-check. Explicitly annotate the property as number | undefined."
    }

findings.title: Only cache devices after successful admission
findings.body: tagDeviceUI adds the device to localCache before CreateOrUpdateDevice checks the limit. When the store returns ErrDeviceLimitReached, that cache entry remains. The next request with the same device ID returns nil from the cache lookup, so Anonymous.Authenticate grants access without checking the limit again. Every rejected device can therefore bypass the limit by retrying, for the 29-minute cache lifetime. Cache only successful admissions, and do not treat an in-flight admission as successful.

findings.title: Requests without a device header bypass the limit
findings.body: The authentication gate relies entirely on TagDevice, but TagDevice returns nil immediately when X-Grafana-Device-Id is absent. An anonymous client can omit this client-controlled header and continue accessing Grafana APIs even when the configured device limit has been reached; no count or admission check runs. Requests subject to the limit need a server-established device identifier or another admission path rather than treating missing tracking information as successful admission.

findings.title: Make counting and admitting a device atomic
findings.body: CountDevices and the subsequent upsert execute in separate database sessions without serialization. Two requests for different new device IDs can both observe a count below deviceLimit and then both insert successfully. For example, with a limit of one and an empty table, concurrent requests can admit multiple devices, which remain eligible for updates afterward. Admission must atomically enforce the count across concurrent requests and Grafana instances.

findings.title: Register device_limit in the default configuration
findings.body: This PR reads device_limit but does not add that key to conf/defaults.ini. Grafana's environment override pass visits keys already present in the loaded INI configuration, before readAuthSettings runs. Consequently, setting GF_AUTH_ANONYMOUS_DEVICE_LIMIT alone in a normal deployment is ignored, and this getter reads zero, silently disabling the limit. Add the key to the default configuration or read it through an environment-aware accessor.

findings.title: Preserve the numeric type of anonymousDeviceLimit
findings.body: The initializer infers this class property as undefined, not number | undefined. The exported runtime config therefore declares that anonymousDeviceLimit can never contain the number supplied by the backend, despite GrafanaConfig declaring that numeric contract. Consumers that narrow the property before using number methods get a never type and cannot type-check. Explicitly annotate the property as number | undefined.
